title: Sliced stabilization ladder and hotfix routing for cross‑plane regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple customers reported generation-quality regressions after a model variant rollout across Hosted, Dedicated and Private planes. Canaries passed in synthetic metrics, but a specific tenant slice experienced hallucinations and truncation under medium token lengths.

Goal: Create a reproducible containment + stabilization ladder that: 1) isolates affected tenant slices quickly, 2) routes affected traffic to a safe fallback variant without interrupting unaffected slices, 3) automates KV-cache reconciliation or pinning to avoid stale-context replays, and 4) provides a clear customer liaison path and hotfix routing for Dedicated/Private customers with restricted control planes.

Scope: This ticket coordinates engineering work (runtime, routing, kvcache), oncall playbook updates, and customer-communication templates. It covers Hosted API fallback wiring, Dedicated pool pinning runbook, and a patched rollback/rollforward flow for Private deployments where control-plane access requires admin coordination.
notes: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage after customer escalation (Acct: Clearwave). Repro steps attached; issue appears for requests with prompt length 120-320 tokens when using model:redwood-v1.2-quantized on GPU-A100 clusters.

2026-03-11 - Daniel Kim: Reproduced locally using tenant-slice replay. Hypothesis: KV-cache eviction misalignment + kernel selector choosing perf-optimized attention kernel that underflows on certain quantization buckets. Created a minimal repro and attached profiler logs.

2026-03-12 - Runtime team (Marta Ivanov): Added a temporary experiment flag to force conservative kernel selection and observed quality restoration for the repro trace. Observed 5-8% latency increase for those buckets. Requesting decision on default policy for safety vs latency.

2026-03-12 - PM (Ravi Menon): Customer impact high; recommended emergency canary to route only impacted tenant slices to legacy kernel until patch validated. Asked for customer communication draft for Clearwave and two other affected customers.

2026-03-13 - Infra (Luis Ortega): For Dedicated pools we can pin specific tenants to older model variant via the reserved-route feature. For Private installs, we'll need an ops-run to toggle model pinning in the customer's control plane; created infra PR to expose tenant-pin API (see attachments).

2026-03-14 - Decision: Enable stabilization-ladder flow: (1) detect anomalous tenant slice via new quality detector (synthetic prompt set + regression thresholds), (2) create ephemeral tenant-specific fallback route to model:redwood-v1.1-stable, (3) enqueue kvcache rewarm/flush job to avoid stale context, (4) if fallback restores quality, schedule canary patch; otherwise escalate to rollback + customer NOC. Runtime will gate conservative kernel selection behind a feature-flag for gradual rollout.
2026-03-14 - Action items assigned: ENG-745322 implement detection + routing automation (assignee: Priya Shah), ENG-745323 implement kvcache rewarm/flush + pin API (assignee: Marco Liu).

2026-03-15 - QA (Sofia Rivera): Starting automated verification run against Clearwave synthetic set; initial run shows 92% pass after conservative kernel, passing our alert thresholds. Will run a 6-hour smoke on Dedicated pools before approving canary.
2026-03-15 - Customer comms: Draft message for Clearwave ready in Confluence; legal reviewed. Support to send once canary shows 2 hours of stable behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Automated detector flags impacted tenant slices with < 3m detection latency
Traffic for flagged slices is routed to fallback model automatically without impact to other slices
KV-cache reconciliation either rewarms or flushes to prevent stale replays for affected tenants
Dedicated pools expose tenant-pin route toggle that can be invoked by oncall within 15 minutes
Private customer plan includes operator checklist to perform pin and rollback with comms template
Canary runs (Hosted + Dedicated) show quality metrics meeting baseline for 6h before wider rollout
risks: Conservative kernel selection increases latency for flagged buckets — tradeoff between cost/latency and correctness
Automatic kvcache flush may transiently increase cold-start token costs and slightly raise latency for rewarm
Private customer rollbacks require coordinated ops window — slower remediation cadence
False positives in detector could unnecessarily route customers to older models
open_questions: What SLO degradation threshold should trigger automatic stabilization ladder vs manual oncall intervention?
Should the conservative kernel be permanently added to kernel selector for specific quantization buckets, or remain behind a feature flag for targeted rollouts?
Do we need an opt-in allowlist for Dedicated customers to accept automated tenant pinning?
recommended_next_steps: Merge infra PR to expose tenant-pin API and deploy to staging (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1890)
Runtime team to push conservative-kernel flag behind rollout service and enable for canary slice
Support to prepare customer comms and schedule ops window for Private customers if pinning required
QA to run 6-hour canary verification on Clearwave + two additional tenants before approval
